hypothesis: Under the existing AVGO downside contract, an equal-weight 0% / 10% post-FY2028 total-revenue-growth distribution is sufficient for AVGO to match or exceed the NVIDIA canonical base-case five-year price IRR.
capital_allocation_importance: The prior deterministic 7.83910862% post-FY2028 AVGO growth assumption was rejected as evidence-backed because dated customer deployment visibility ends in 2029. A probability-weighted comparison can avoid pretending FY2030-FY2031 growth is known, but only if the probability hurdle required to beat NVDA is explicit rather than invented.

precommitted_decision_rule.USE: The equal-weight 0% / 10% distribution produces AVGO expected IRR at least 1 percentage point above NVDA at 25x, 35x, and 45x terminal Price/FCF.
precommitted_decision_rule.CONDITION: The expected-return difference is mixed across multiples or all three differences are within +/-1 percentage point.
precommitted_decision_rule.REJECT: The equal-weight distribution leaves AVGO at least 1 percentage point below NVDA at all three terminal multiples.
precommitted_decision_rule.UNVERIFIED: The canonical AVGO stress outputs, NVIDIA comparator, or current source identity cannot be verified.

primary_evidence.source: Broadcom Q3 FY2026 results and Q4 guidance
primary_evidence.fact: Q3 AI semiconductor revenue was 16.7B USD, up 221% year over year; Q4 AI semiconductor revenue guidance was 21.7B USD, up 236% year over year.
10GW deployment is targeted to start in 2H 2026 and complete by end of 2029.
The multi-year, multi-generation MTIA partnership is explicitly planned through 2029.
The AI XPV Platform targets more than 20GW of Broadcom XPU/networking-enabled compute capacity through 2028; 35B USD is infrastructure transaction value, not Broadcom revenue.

method.type: Probability-hurdle valuation comparison using already-validated canonical scenario outputs.
method.why_no_forecast_probability_is_invented: No public point-in-time evidence verified in this run supplies an empirical probability for FY2030-FY2031 AVGO growth. Therefore 50/50 is used only as a neutral robustness benchmark, not as a claim that either scenario has 50% real-world probability.
method.simple_benchmark: NVDA canonical base-case IRR at the same terminal Price/FCF multiple.
method.alternative: Report the implied minimum probability on the 10% AVGO growth scenario instead of asserting a probability forecast.

benchmark_comparison.benchmark: NVDA canonical base-case five-year price IRR.
benchmark_comparison.simple_probability_benchmark: AVGO 50% weight on 0% post-FY2028 growth and 50% weight on 10% growth.
benchmark_comparison.result: The equal-weight AVGO expected IRR is 1.81575045 to 2.04225827 percentage points below NVDA across 25x, 35x, and 45x. AVGO needs about 78.71% probability on the 10% growth branch, versus 21.29% on the 0% branch, merely to match NVDA under this binary support.
benchmark_comparison.interpretation: The probability-weighted model does not rescue AVGO without a strong prior that FY2029-FY2031 total revenue growth will be near 10% rather than 0%. Current dated customer announcements do not cover FY2030-FY2031, so that 78.71% probability cannot be promoted to an evidence-backed input.

risk_metrics.reason: This is a point-in-time forward fundamental scenario comparison, not a realized return-series backtest.
material_risks: The 115B / 230B USD AI semiconductor figures are management outlook, not realized revenue.
The 0% and 10% scenario supports are canonical sensitivity points, not an empirical forecast distribution.
Public customer deployment commitments verified here end by 2029, leaving FY2030-FY2031 demand probability unobserved.
FCF margin compression, dilution, and non-AI decline remain model stresses rather than issuer guidance.
NVDA comparator also contains forward assumptions and is not a realized-return benchmark.

decision.reason: Under the neutral 50/50 robustness benchmark, AVGO remains more than 1 percentage point below NVDA at all three common terminal multiples, satisfying the precommitted REJECT rule. Matching NVDA requires about 78.71% weight on the 10% post-FY2028 growth branch, a probability not supported by dated FY2030-FY2031 customer evidence.
decision.portfolio_implication: Do not overweight AVGO relative to NVDA using a probability-weighted story unless the assumed probability of sustained post-FY2028 growth is stated explicitly and supported. Treat 78.71% as a conviction hurdle for the 0%/10% binary support, not as a forecast probability.

implementation.usage_rule: Keep scenario probabilities explicit. Never silently assign an empirical probability to FY2030-FY2031 AVGO growth until point-in-time evidence supports it.

remaining_uncertainty: The actual FY2030-FY2031 growth distribution is not observable from current dated customer commitments. Future contracts, renewals, product generations, cancellations, capacity additions, or pricing could materially change the probability hurdle.
next_hypothesis: Using historical Broadcom annual revenue downside and forecast-error base rates from issuer filings, rather than a neutral 50/50 benchmark, produces an empirical prior that places at least 78.71% probability on a post-FY2028 growth outcome equivalent to 10% versus 0%.
